messages:
incident-bot: Pager — P1: Customer NimbleHealth (private VPC deployment) experiencing widespread request failures to inference endpoints. Affected: dedicated pool 'nimble-dedicated-1'. Trigger: high 502/504 rate from NLB. Paging on-call.

alice_sre: saw this, I'm on it. 502s across all routes to the customer's API gateway.

brian_network: checking the NLB target health and security groups now. Ping me if you need SG tweaks.

sarah_se: Customer reported spikes ~09:02 UTC after a config deploy. They say some pods aren't receiving traffic.

mike_netops: NLB shows many targets as Unhealthy, healthchecks failing with TCP reset. Backend instances still healthy on our end for other tenants.

jordan_oncall: taking lead — I'm going to confirm scope (ingress vs egress) and start impact assessment.

leah_support: CustOps (cust-ops-nimble) pinged: "Most inference calls return 502, some succeed intermittently. This started right after we updated our DNS to point to the new NLB. We rolled back DNS but issue persisted." They want ETA.

cust-ops-nimble: (from customer): "We reverted our ALB config but still see failures. Can you confirm your NLB IPs and SGs?"

alice_sre: initial hypothesis: NLB -> ALB handoff mismatch or security group on customer VPC side blocking new NLB CIDR after the swap. Also possible target group healthcheck path mismatch after model rollout.

brian_network: confirmed: NLB frontends healthy, but the NLB target group is showing >50% unhealthy due to 504s while probing backend ALB. Flow logs show the customer NACL rejecting some source CIDRs (our egress IP set). Looks like the customer's SG/NACL changes during their DNS flip.

mike_netops: customer is on a private VPC with AWS-managed NLB in front of our peering. If their NACL is blocking our egress IPs intermittently, that would explain the flapping.

sarah_se: Isolate impact: only their dedicated pool nimble-dedicated-1 and traffic routed to region eu-west-1. Other customers unaffected.

jordan_oncall: current action items:
- Confirm final set of egress IPs we used for the NLB (brian)
- Ask customer to whitelist those IPs in SG/NACL and reduce NACL stateless restrictions temporarily (sarah + cust)
- Temporarily route traffic through backup public egress via bastion/proxy to validate (alice)
- If needed, perform a quick rollback of recent target group change (kevin to prepare)

brian_network: egress IP list: 34.207.12.11, 34.207.12.12, 18.197.45.9 (these are NAT egress for the peering NAT GW). Sending to cust contact now. Also seeing SYN-RSTs back from their side.

cust-ops-nimble: received IPs, applying to SG now. Will keep NACL permissive for next 10 minutes and report back.

leah_support: FYI: customer business impact = degraded inference — high priority, trying to pull executives into the loop.

(1 minute later)

cust-ops-nimble: updated SG/NACL, confirmed allowed 34.207.12.0/24, but still seeing 502s.

alice_sre: running endpoint test via temporary proxy with our egress IP 52.23.99.101 to confirm path.

alice_sre: test through proxy -> 200 OK. So when we egress from that proxy IP, traffic succeeds. Points to inconsistent route/SG behavior depending on which egress IP is used.

brian_network: digging into NAT GW health and AZ distribution. One NAT GW in eu-west-1b had high connection tracking exhaustion after the deploy — could have been returning RSTs. We're seeing asymmetric egress IPs between NLB and probe clients.

mike_netops: immediate mitigation: toggle NLB cross-zone balancing to even out targets and force new egress IP selection, and scale NAT GW (create another NAT in eu-west-1c) to spread connections.

jordan_oncall: go ahead with NAT GW scale and NLB toggle. Communicate to customer that we may see a few seconds of additional failures during the flip.

kevin_eng: preparing rollback of recent target group config; will be ready if NAT changes don't stabilize within 5 minutes.

(2 minutes later)

brian_network: NAT GW scaled, new NAT created in eu-west-1c. Cross-zone balancing toggled. Monitoring target health.

sarah_se: target health starting to recover — healthy count rising from 40% -> 78%.

cust-ops-nimble: seeing steady success rate now. Thank you. We still saw 1-2 requests fail but overall looks much better.

jordan_oncall: status update to execs: customer-impacting incident (P1) — root cause: egress IP/NAT GW capacity exhaustion combined with customer-side NACL tightening during a DNS swap. Mitigation: scaled NAT GW and adjusted NLB balancing; asked customer to whitelist full egress CIDR for stability. Rolling to monitoring for 30min.

leah_support: noted for post-incident: coordinate with Customer Ops to provide recommended whitelist CIDR blocks and runbook for DNS flips.

kevin_eng: keeping rollback ready for 10 more minutes, but no longer needed.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigated at 09:18 UTC. On-call: jordan_oncall. Follow-up: postmortem required. Assign to alice_sre + brian_network + cust-ops-nimble for next steps.

alice_sre: will draft postmortem and include a recommended checklist for customers doing DNS swaps and dedicated pool swaps (NAT capacity check, full CIDR whitelist, TTL guidance).
